findings.title: RPC sends before deadline and response-transaction admission
findings.observed: request(value) writes to child.stdin before next() checks the absolute deadline. next() returns queued messages without checking the deadline or matching the outgoing transaction. An expired request can therefore reach the child and a new request can receive an old queued response.
reproduction: Use the exact frozen python-rpc module with a pureNode child that reports ready, ignoresSIGTERM and writes any received step to a temporary sentinel.
After a300ms deadline, call request(step B2) at350ms. The Promise rejects for deadline but the child actually receives step B2 and writes the sentinel.

In a second pureNode child, enqueue an unsolicited stepped A1 after ready. request(step B2) sends B2, then returns the queued A1 object. The current controller rejects mismatched kind/arm/update, but has already dispatched new work before rejecting.
Both probes explicitly await stop and SIGKILL cleanup; no productionservice/model/Torch is involved. Root-provided externalPython expired-send red evidence independently agrees.
findings.impact: The absolute soft budget/transaction boundary is violated before computation. Controller checks prevent treating the tested mismatched response as a completed valid update, and the outer hard bound remains, but they cannot retract an already sent optimizer request. This is a resource/admission defect and partial-update ambiguity, not proof that an actual invalid mature result was accepted.
findings.recommendation: Check deadline/state and outstanding/queued response admission before stdin.write, allow at most one explicit transaction, bind responses to request IDs or validated expected kind/arm/update, reject stale/unsolicited responses without sending more work, and route all failure paths through bounded termination/exit join.

findings.title: Python independent entry lacks complete authority and tree validation before Torch import
findings.observed: The entry compares os.getppid only to a caller-supplied value, not an authenticated officialNode identity. Lease contract/snapshot/anchor bindings and realpath/closed-tree semantics are omitted. It checks only anchor.initialEntryHash rather than the actual original ledger genesis/full hashchain. The reservation balance loop runs after importing torch/training_core and merely totals matching reserve/settle rows.
reproduction: Copy only the frozen service to a personal/tmp fixture and replace the one fixed repository literal to redirect all canonical I/O into that fixture; preserve guard control flow. Use only tiny sentinel modules named torch/training_core/mature_protocol; no real Torch library or model is imported.
With no6000reservation, the sentinel torch import executes and only then does the entry reject for missing reservation.
With a one-line forged reserve6000 ledger having invalidgenesis/hashchain, the service reaches ready.
With a manifest-external torch.py beside the service, its sentinel code is imported and the service reaches ready; the entry never performs full-tree closure or realpath-parent validation.

With the official-parent field set to an unrelatedPID and lease contract/snapshot fields deliberatelywrong while parent_pid is the real caller PID, it also reaches ready. Each ready case then exits on deliberate stdinEOF; no init or optimizer request is sent.
findings.impact: The independently callable Python boundary does not establish the pre-heavy-import authority promised by the request. The normal frozenNode route has stronger checks, but it does not replace a standalone fail-closed Python guard. The tests demonstrate absent checks in redirected fixtures; they do not assert that real canonical files were forged or an actual scientific job was bypassed.
findings.recommendation: Before any output marker, Torch or research-training import, reuse a strict frozen verifier/authority helper to bind the actual officialNode parent identity, canonical receipt+contract+snapshot, complete lease fields/anchorSHA, original pinned genesis and full ledger chain, active exact6000reservation/once-only state, interpreter identity and full realpath/closed-tree source closure. Preserve the explicit scope that installed externalTorch is not wholly copied.
findings.probeQualification: Only the canonical repository literal was redirected in the copied service. Fake receipts/ledgers/leases and sentinel import modules exist only under/private/tmp. Four mechanicalPython processes ran, zero realTorch imports, zero models/updates, zero real canonical writes.

findings.title: finish has no hard exit bound or SIGKILL escalation

locations.symbol: finish waits exited after one SIGTERM

findings.observed: finish() ends stdin and sends oneSIGTERM after2seconds, then awaits exited without using the absolute RPC deadline or escalating toSIGKILL. If the child ignoresSIGTERM and holds a handle, finish never returns and the caller never enters its finally/stop cleanup.
reproduction: Start the exact frozen RPC with a pureNode child that reports ready and closed, retains an interval and deliberately ignoresSIGTERM.
Give RPC an absolute1500ms deadline, then await finish after the valid close response. At3000ms finish is stillpending and the child recorded ignoredSIGTERM.
An explicit separate stop call is required toSIGKILL it after another2seconds. The probe awaits exit and leaves no child. NoPython/Torch/model is run.
findings.impact: The promised bounded normal-close/exit join is absent for an unresponsive child. The controller can wait until the outer hard timeout; that timeout kills the primaryNode rather than guaranteeing the learner child has exited, so closing budget/lease first can leave computation unaccounted for. This is distinct from the expired-send defect.
findings.recommendation: Make finish honor an absolute shutdown deadline and always perform boundedSIGTERM-to-SIGKILL escalation plus awaited exit; ensure controller/hard-timeout cleanup owns its learner subprocess before settlement and lease removal. Retain the requirement of successful normal exit for a completed report.
